title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
Microsoft is reportedly offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees. This move affects over a quarter of their global workforce and is aimed at cutting costs as the company shifts its focus toward AI integration.

In California, Mark Zuckerberg has reached a deal with Meta that keeps him in the state. The company’s board was concerned that his potential departure over a proposed wealth tax could derail their AI goals. A new stock agreement has been put in place to help him manage the financial impact if that tax measure becomes law.

In legal news, a US judge has ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by December 11 regarding his 10 billion dollar lawsuit against the BBC. If he does not cooperate with the discovery process, the judge has threatened to dismiss the case entirely.

On the policy front, UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves has unveiled her first budget. It includes a 100 pound credit for energy bills and a new tax on banks, aimed at addressing the cost of living while managing economic uncertainty.

Finally, Apple users have a new update. iOS 27.2 is now rolling out, bringing Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo. The update also adds an Edge Light feature designed to brighten faces during video calls.
cta: Get the full picture and stay informed on HEADLINNE.com.
